assumptions.original: The sample measure $\mu$ is finite. Time is nonnegative and the fixed horizon $T$ may equal zero. The coordinate set $I$ and noise index set $J$ are finite, with decidable equality on $I$. The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time. Each drift coordinate has integrable time sections for $\mu$-almost every sample. Each noise entry is a strongly progressive integrand with $L^2(\mu\otimes\ell_T)$ membership, where $\ell_T=\mathrm{Leb}|_{[0,T]}$. The Euclidean path $X$ is almost surely continuous on $[0,T]$ and almost surely stays in the set $K$ at all horizon times. The ambient test $f$ is $C^2$ at each point of $K$.
assumptions.reconstructed: mu is finite. Each eta_ij is strongly progressive with (omega,t)↦eta_ij(t,omega) in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). For every i, b_i(·,omega) is lambda_T-integrable for mu-a.e. omega. X(·,omega) is continuous on [0,T] mu-a.e. and, on a mu-full set, X(t,omega)∈K for every t≤T. At every w∈K, f is C² at w in the ambient Euclidean space. There is no compactness assumption on K, no Brownian motion assumption, and no progressivity assumption on b or X.
assumptions.evidence: Full-module binder and definition audit: No Brownian, b-progressive, X-measurable or K-compact binder appears. Product L2 supplies hProducts; hD/hH are continuous along the chosen compact-time path; the private bounded-product lemma and finite basis expansions discharge both integrability claims.

conclusion.original: Let $v$ be the vector with the given scalar drift rows and $\sigma_j$ the vector with the $j$th given noise column. Both generator terms displayed below are integrable in time for almost every sample. Formula: Df(X_t)[v_t],\qquad \tfrac12\sum_{j\in J}D^2f(X_t)[\sigma_{j,t},\sigma_{j,t}]\quad\in L^1(\ell_T)\quad\text{a.s.}
